title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: The navigation history keeps the way back, records where your cursor really is, and the test source set filter works on Windows again.

highlights.title: Back keeps the way back
highlights.description: Pressing Back within half a second of a jump could overwrite the entry you were returning to with the destination you had just left. The way back was gone, and pressing Back again went forward.

highlights.title: Your cursor, not line 0
highlights.description: Switching to a tab you already had open filed the visit at line 0, because no selection event fires for a file you have already seen. The entry now starts from the cursor the editor already carries.

highlights.title: Test source sets on Windows
highlights.description: The filter compared a path written with backslashes against segments written with slashes, so no file was ever recognised as a test file and the rule ran backwards.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Go to Definition no longer treats a directory that merely starts like a test source set as one. It kept a private copy of the path check, written before the bounded comparison landed.
Moving through the history closes any pending refinement, so a late event from the previous jump can no longer reach an entry it does not own.
